story_mappings.introduction: Follow Szxvu’s silver and gem commissions, understand their active-accounting payment limits, and use the fence, mound and temple clues to trace the exact material sources. The journal keeps useful preparation services separate from the guarded spectacles request, ambient scenes, dangerous guardian behavior and Winterhaven’s memory continuation.
orientation: Active, ready accounting is required for discovery, visible encounters, journals and new achievement/daily credit. Discovering Kobold Settlement has its own achievement. All four native exchanges are explained here. Three supporting services do not count toward zone completion; the spectacles request retains one achievement candidate whose paid offering is guarded. None is a daily candidate.

The two useful progressions are nuggets → silver blocks → shield, and statue gems + corpse frames → spectacles. Each declared exchange stays independent. Inspection and producer receipts are optional; exact supplied materials skip earlier personal history. Current custody does not establish a first original acquisition, a personal kill or safe source access.

Szxvu at 1406 asks 10 platinum and eight nuggets for one block, then 170 platinum and two blocks for the shield. Two self-produced blocks use sixteen nuggets and two separate smelting fees. The spectacles recipe asks for 20 platinum, the exact gems and frames. These recipes cannot accept mixed coin-and-item payments with accounting active; gathering materials does not remove that guard.

Szxvu also receives a smith handler dynamically from the tradeskill table. Its ten armor recipes use the separate ore kinds and a generated object, rather than the local nugget/block recipes. The forge command is disabled with accounting active, including its menu. It is not a working alternative for these commissions or a rod-reassembly route.

Miners and leaders at 1495 and 1498 declare five nugget resets with a normal global live-copy limit five. The smelt wants eight. Saved-item reload, ordinary resets and forced repops can differ; the source audit does not establish a played eight-nugget collection or daily-renewal route. The journal can count exact supplied loose nuggets without promising their availability.

Gem inspection names the same input and output kind, not a guaranteed return of the original item identity. The later spectacles recipe is checked first and shares the gems. With no frames, inspection can remain the matching route; with the matching frames, its unsupported fee can block that route. Do not make inspection a required stage or keep handing gems over to force progress.

From Surface 622130, travel north to forest trail 1400, then north toward the fence at 1462. The iron gate needs Gwark’s key. TUG the root switch at 1463 or its counterpart at 1469 to clear the reciprocal blocked fence passage. This opens a route, without creating a quest receipt.

The settlement can also be entered from Winterhaven 55402 southwest to 1402 through the foreign Incarnate Evil loading area. There is no declared ordinary reverse exit from 1402 to that room. Deep cavern 1542 connects east with Underdark 816080 west. Foreign discovery and completion retain their own ownership.

Gwark’s key fits the house door 1433 north ↔ 1434 south and the perimeter gate 1462 north ↔ 1468 south. The shaman’s key fits mound door 1425 north ↔ 1456 south; the mound desk holds the note about the temple word. The pantry trapdoor 1436 down ↔ 1455 up starts closed without a key lock.

From pond 1424, the downward muddy hole enters 1445. At 1449, PULL the bar switch to clear the blocked east passage to 1470; its western return door resets closed without a lock. Continue east to 1471, down to 1472, east to 1473 and down to temple 1474. Normal rubble clearing and actual arrival are separate from recorded story acceptance.

At temple 1476, static warrior corpse 1463 contains the spectacle frames and language journal. The statue at 1478 wears the gem eyes and has a custom stone-pile death handler. Reading the journal or recovering gear supplies clues, without automatically recording a learned language, first-source acquisition, kill or corpse recovery.

The altar at 1481 has the eastern bone door to tomb 1482, with magic-key marker -2 and final keyword i>|uub. The note, parchment and language journal explain a translation puzzle. Shared speech checks the raw supplied word and unlocks matching reciprocal locks; it does not automatically open the door or prove the language was learned. Jkyl’s east barrier is a separate live actor obstacle.

The restored temple handlers use their actual reset rooms: Jkyl at altar 1481, golems at tomb 1482, demon at pit 1484. Jkyl’s west command sends the actor to the pit; the demon can pull an eligible player from ledge 1483 and start combat, and can block upward escape. Actor presence and command/periodic conditions matter. Neither arrival nor narration proves survival or a successful escape.

Tomb 1482 contains the sarcophagus with a tablet half, gear and the imported Kobold Settlement memory 55440. The other tablet is on the pit demon. The imported rune-covered stone 358 uses shared epic TOUCH settlement, separately from journal request credit; visiting or hearing it hum does not prove an accepted award. Rod of Rulership prototypes and four same-named pieces have lore, but the reviewed resets, native quests and smith recipes provide no local piece supply or reassembly endpoint. Treat that as an incomplete integration lead until builder intent and an actual route are established.

The tomb’s imported memory continues to the Kobold Settlement ambassador in Winterhaven for two declared item rewards and 1000000 copper. This is the existing foreign memory request. Obtaining the memory or visiting the tomb does not complete Winterhaven’s offering or discover that zone.

No room declares a current or chance-fall property; pit danger is driven by the native guardian handlers and ordinary vertical travel. The pond uses ordinary water movement rules, with BOAT boots as one declared source of support. Inns, recovery flags, room names and carried equipment do not promise safe travel or reset renewal.

story_mappings.introduction: Investigate the Darvanu's hold over Quietus Quay through officer contracts and pirate accounts. Follow the suggested mission route or deliver proof you already have.
orientation: Meet the thin duergar on the barracks path and the officers farther along the paths. Credentials unlock briefings; the four mission deliveries earn separate accomplishments.
The drow mission needs its note and Aresliean's head together. Rodev's sword and Eckraldu's staff have separate lieutenants. The captain's seal and dagger routes explain his bloodstone mission.
Empty badges before offering them. A badge is a container, and its contents are not returned by a briefing. Secure any captain materials you need before his final delivery.
Pirate rumors are leads; Aresliean and the captain may be difficult to locate. Supplied proof items are accepted without a recorded briefing or personal kill.

The one-eyed bartender has a separate random world-quest service. New paid requests are currently unavailable; use quest to view an existing task. The shipwright, crew hall, inn and shops have their own availability rules.
Optional exploration includes the estate's containers, hidden Golden Lyre instrument shop and bat shrine. These routes do not complete an officer mission.

story_mappings.introduction: Discover the Englehardt family's history, return the pianist's missing music and the handmaid's rattle, and bring Lord Englehardt both demon proofs for his vault key. These are three independent accepted requests. Clues and shared doors explain the route; exact loose materials prepare a turn-in. New progress requires active, ready accounting.
orientation: The Forgotten Mansion leads from an abandoned garden and house into haunted caverns, a cathedral, demon chambers and a guarded vault. Discovery records arrival. It does not guarantee safe access to every room, a present giver or available supplies.

ASK gardener about key, door, family, name or secrets. The gardener points toward a desk and the family-name clue. The gate and front-door plaque name Englehardt. These leads help explain the house; individual ASK keywords do not award achievements or become required personal history.

A small jodani key is declared inside the closed wooden desk in the dusty basement. It fits the front door and can break on use. Both this desk and the elegant bedroom desk are closed containers without native locks. Opening a shared desk is access, and carrying a supplied exact item also fits a request.

ASK pianist about piano, music, phoenix or rise. The old musical paper is inside the elegant desk in the southeast corner of the master bedroom. Return it for a black opal ring and a diary entry about the family's experiments. The response explains how the library leads below; reading a reward or owning a ring does not itself prove the request was accepted.

In the dark library, SAY englehardt to unlock and reveal the eastern stone door, then open it to enter the cavern. This is an actual shared magic-word door. Another player's prior opening may provide access. Your own discovery of the written name, pianist turn-in or SAY history is not an extra native requirement for the later quests.

ASK handmaid about baby, crying, child or cry. The exact rattle is declared in a pouch on a humanoid skeleton in the cavern tunnel. This skeleton is a container rather than a live child or a freshly created corpse. Return the rattle for platinum wristwear. The response describes quieting the child; the native room descriptions still contain crying, so the journal records the accepted return without claiming a permanent world-state change.

ASK englehardt about life, experiment, quest, offer, strong, vault, gaultair or tyrlos. Bring the bloody head of Gaultair AND the horn of Tyrlos together. Gaultair and Tyrlos declare these exact proof objects; supplied proofs also fit. Lord Englehardt rewards the complete bundle with his golden vault key and experience. One proof alone, a similarly named trophy or his key alone is not acceptance.

The route below has locked and hidden doors, lava passages and falls. An obsidian key leads into the cathedral; a key in the podium leads toward Gaultair; Gaultair's living-magma key fits a hidden northwest passage toward Tyrlos. Current access and the normal movement, search and door rules matter. The journal does not require a personal sequence of key pickups, kills or unlocks.

Englehardt's key opens the first local vault door. The red and gold dragons declare different keys for the later golden and platinum doors. A separate Winterhaven passage enters the treasure room from outside this local chain. Arrival at the treasure room therefore does not prove that you completed Englehardt's request or personally opened every vault door.

The treasure room declares an epic runestone and a dragon-carried memory of The Forgotten Mansion. The stone has its own eligible group reward and committed zone-touch process. The memory can be offered to the Mansion ambassador in Winterhaven for that city's reward. Those are separate outcomes; neither substitutes for a local quest receipt or proves that every demon was personally defeated.

Tyrlos also declares a green vapor with its own shield, curse and equipment behavior. Its effects do not remove the house's curse or complete Englehardt's offering. Current loose custody prepares each request; worn, held, nested, spent or handed-away supplies do not. Three accepted stories contribute three achievements and potential dailies. Fresh stock, giver availability and active, ready accounting govern new progress.

story_mappings.introduction: Meet the woodland folk, follow the forrestal’s leads and explore the elemental fragments and ether tower. Three independent offerings record accepted outcomes; the six-plaque treasure puzzle is a separate exploration route. New discovery and progress require active, ready accounting.
orientation: Enter from the animal path through the forest. The protector stands at the eastern entrance. Woodland fairies, sprites, brownies, koalas and the dryad have different leads. ASK a nearby person about one of their listed topics; a recognized reply can reveal that contact, without making every keyword a separate achievement.

Find the forrestal, who starts in the northwest maple grove and can wander. Ask groves, sprite, dark, rift, rowans and heal for the damaged-grove story. He accepts two exact keys for experience, or the cube of ethereal matter for a greenstone earring and experience. These are three independent deliveries; no earlier personal discussion or offering receipt is required.

The cloudy key starts on the ground in the maple grove, and the black key starts on the ground in the dogwood grove. Each fits a different upper tower door. Use the key for access before spending it on the forrestal if you want that route. A supplied key fits too; an already-open shared path does not prove your own unlocking.

The twisted rowan grove leads west into separate earth, water, fire and air fragments. Follow the sprites’ realm and sanctum clues. Each fragment has two different guardian keys and a sanctum route; the exact keys and doors differ. Combat, key recovery and travel are separate from the forrestal’s accepted deliveries.

Earth uses the gravel and slate keys; water uses seashell and coral; fire uses igneous and magma; air uses glass and crystal. The guardian equipment or carried stock supplies these keys when legitimately available. Current possession can prepare access, but does not prove a personal kill or first acquisition from its original source.

Water routes include deep water and underwater rooms; air routes include rooms without ground, and fire routes include fire-plane terrain. Native movement, breath, flight, levitation, mounts and hazards still apply. The blue seashell has a worn waterbreathing effect; the fairy-dust pouch explicitly does not grant flight. Neither item is a compulsory forrestal offering.

The four sanctums and the two upper tower rooms are the intended plaque branches. Five copies of the same runed pedestal and one black pedestal are closed display containers, without a lock. Open the display case and examine its actual contents. Available stock depends on what has already been recovered and whether the grove has renewed.

Climb the baobab to the ether tower. The five climbing rooms have different native fall settings, and the tower contains wombats and an ether wraith. The wraith’s equipment includes the actual cube of ethereal matter. It is an offering item, not a container you must open, and it appears before the final six-plaque treasure chamber.

The cloudy key fits the upper door from the northeastern tower corner to the ethereal sanctum; the black key fits the other upper door to the empty tower. Those rooms are intended to supply the cloudy and black plaques. Returning either key for experience consumes it, so a reward receipt cannot replace access stock.

The six plaque keys fit the northern corridor in this order: stone, silver, gold, crystal, cloudy, black. Each plaque carries part of the final riddle. The last elemental door answers to SAY nothing beside it; then OPEN it if closed. Speech ability and native shared door state matter. Reading, saying the word and opening a door do not currently create personal puzzle-completion receipts.

The final chamber holds a small black cube, a fixed closed container distinct from the ether wraith’s offering. Its reset children are a black wand and a jagged obsidian dagger. The dagger has its own combat effects. The room’s epic stone and memory trophy follow separate rules; none is an input to the forrestal’s three deliveries.

The enchanted valley can be reached through downward exits from the air route. Its lady has equipment and lore, without a native delivery contract. The northern archway returns to the winding path through the glades through an ordinary exit. The bubbling spring is an object with a DRINK spring effect, not a quest turn-in.

Returning the ethereal cube rewards the earring and experience, then retires that forrestal. His reply says he may heal the grove and will tell the dryad; the current contract does not restore rooms, escort anyone or record a personal rescue. The earring’s worn effect is protection from fire. Base experience amounts still follow native capped and frozen recipient reward rules.

These three deliveries are potential dailies only when the real giver and legitimate proof stock are available. Current stock and wandering or retired givers can limit availability; the journal does not guarantee renewed supplies. No new discovery, journal or completion credit is available without active, ready accounting.

story_mappings.introduction: Explore several independent forests, inns, ruins and outposts under one Mini Zones journal. Follow three accepted requests or stories and four supporting armor recipes. Current materials and earlier exchanges explain possible routes, without requiring personal recovery. Active, ready accounting is required.
orientation: The ruined city, Broken Blade tavern and ruined outpost each have working Surface Realm approaches. Discovering one part opens this shared journal; it does not prove you have visited every mini-area. Several other boundary exits point to absent rooms and need a reviewed repair.

At the Broken Blade tavern, the dishwasher in the kitchen complains about waittress. Her actual tip jar is carried by the young waitress in the dining room. The accepted jar delivery reveals a cutpurse clue, without an item, money or experience reward.

Upstairs, the enchanted eastern door accepts the spoken word cutpurse. Speech unlocks it, after which opening the door and travelling through it are separate actions. The guild and fence beneath the tavern have no additional static quest terminal.

In the ruined city, ask the groaning spirit and forgotten knight about driedel. The knight also responds to worach. A parchment addressed to him releases his current appearance and supplies a blue-green strip; there is no implemented Gaffin escort or king-defeat finale.

The secret downward passage between the tower and intact building reaches a chamber with a black wall. Enter that wall for the Maze of Souls. From its entry, east, south, east, east, west, south, east, east reaches the secret passage. Continue east and south twice to the magical cache.

The pale revenant in that cache carries a small closed satchel with the release parchment. Open the accessible bag and take the actual letter. Return through the maze and white-wall exit; searching, reading or entering the maze alone does not deliver the letter.

Restore the silver sword with one silvery-blue strip from the skulk, one blue-green strip from the knight, one silvery-green strip from the Bodak, and the hidden golden hilt in the musk creeper's bulb. Three same-named strips are still different kinds.

The old wise man lives in a forest hut reached through the hole in the city wall. Offer all four pieces together. A supplied set skips any earlier producer history. The sword has a separate wielded combat power; receiving it does not prove the power triggered or affected an enemy.

The well-kept shop has a concealed locked panel. One unseen servant carries its tiny golden key; the panel holds two helpful potions. This preparation is optional, and is distinct from the sword pieces and the released knight's receipt.

At the ruined outpost, the quartermaster stocks ghostly sleeves, pants, gloves and boots. The battlemaster above the sparring hall describes four actual upgrades, each requiring its matching base, five huge blood crystals and 400 platinum. The payment recipes are currently unavailable.

Huge blood crystals have ground sources across the Surface Realm. Five separate crystals and the matching ghostly piece must be ready together for each recipe. Completing an armor service earns its own output, without a story or daily achievement.

The outpost's hidden storage niche holds a durethium key for the torturer's hidden lockbox. The burnt cell has a secret western crawlspace. Key access, lockbox loot and the armor recipes remain independent routes.

The Elvengrove tree doorway uses an oaken key from the wayhouse traveller. Its ancient desk uses a different metallic loop worn by the dryad princess. The current charm and teleport behavior needs further qualification before a personal rescue objective.

The wayhouse, pond, minotaur home, worm nest, inn and ruined city offer independent exploration. Names, drawings, companion plaques, a black monolith and gambling furnishings are lore leads; they do not create automatic learned-topic, game-win or cleared-area achievements.

The inn reception sells an obsidian room key; the actual rental room is upstairs. The wayhouse pet service draws from the adjacent barn rather than the separately labelled storage room. Pet purchases, rentals and claims are unavailable pending payment qualification.

The potash miner at the tavern bar hosts a separate random world-quest service. The nearby elderly bartender does not have that assignment. Those generated tasks retain their own quest system and are not extra static Mini Zones stories.

story_mappings.introduction: Investigate why Septimus’s tribe has stopped travelling. Present the two other-planar shards for his collateral ring, then return the two distinct heads and that ring for the crown of Winduin. The journal separates clues, current supplies and accepted exchanges.
orientation: The camp connects to four Surface rooms in Calimshan: go SOUTH from 582095 to 6203, EAST from 582494 to 6221, WEST from 582496 to 6227, or NORTH from 582895 to 6246. The reverse exits return to the Surface. The wagons form a circle around the bonfire; closed wagon doors still need OPEN under the game’s existing rules.

Ask the wandering Cimmerian purpose or cimmerian; ask the blacksmith work; ask Septimus fate or future. These five existing keywords select three responses. Septimus’s response is heard around the room; hearing it does not record an exchange or teach a fighting skill.

The blacksmith in wagon 6210 starts asleep. WAKE blacksmith may let you ask about work if the game permits it. Waking or speaking to him is a clue route, not a required journal achievement. Septimus waits in wagon 6212, reached NORTHEAST from 6218.

Rellius’s hidden journal is declared on the floor of storage wagon 6236. When present and revealed by native SEARCH, LOOK page1 and LOOK page2 provide his suspicions and last investigation. READ page1/page2 uses the same inspection path. Carrying the journal alone does not prove you read those pages, and this journal does not award reading or rescue credit.

For Septimus’s first exchange, gather one exact other-planar wood shard and one exact other-planar iron shard. The tree-like creature in 6208 and the iron creature in 6240 are their native holders. The shards are hidden items; reveal and obtain actual live stock under the game’s rules. Having a wooden training sword, examining the bonfire or holding Rellius’s body does not supply either shard.

Have both shards loose together, then offer a matching shard to Septimus. The accounting hand-in selects and consumes the complete exact bundle for the hallowed Cimmerian ring. Gifts of matching legitimate materials fit without your own creature-kill or clue-reading history. The receipt records the exchange, not how you obtained the evidence.

For the second exchange, carry the shaman’s exact head, the conjurer’s different head and the exact collateral ring loose together. Offer a matching head or the ring to Septimus; the accounting hand-in selects and consumes the whole bundle for the diamond crown of Winduin. A blue or green camp ring does not substitute. Remove a worn collateral ring before offering it.

The shaman in 6208 and the conjurer in 6240 are declared carrying their respective heads even while alive. These are supplied quest items, not a CARVE recipe. Matching supplied heads and ring fit without your own first-exchange or combat record. Both heads share the keyword head, but two copies of one head do not replace the other exact head.

The heads are hidden, transient and no-rent-marked. Dropping them on the floor can arm immediate decay under the game’s item rules. Keep actual materials available for the offering; earlier receipts never replace heads or a ring that were spent, dropped, lost or given away.

Septimus’s crown exchange narrates the camp’s relief and removes that NPC instance. It does not record a personal stranger kill, creature liberation, Rellius recovery or the camp moving away. A crown can also come from a CHAOS starter kit; owning one does not prove this exchange.

Rellius’s hidden body at 6240 is a fixed container prop with a declared training sword inside, not a normal corpse or a rescue endpoint. The blacksmith’s vanished-weapons story, ancient instructors, infirmary and training wagon have no additional local accepted craft, healing, escort or lesson quest. The bonfire’s unburning logs are an inspectable clue, not an implemented new producer or survival objective.

Native resets declare possible materials, not guaranteed live stock. Active accounting currently refuses zone item reset issuance; both exchanges need legitimate existing or supplied materials. Actual renewal still needs qualification before these potential daily quests can promise reliable availability.

story_mappings.introduction: Explore the Court's four seasonal favors, distinct admission tokens and independent brook, soul, stone and lost-wand requests. Active, ready accounting is required. Current proof and accepted deliveries remain separate from first recovery, seasonal rituals, safe access and a personal audience with the Muse.
orientation: Enter the twisted path from the surface and examine the stone arch. The enchanted arch responds to enter, leading into the seasonal forest; its poetic inscription is lore, without a reviewed learned-word quest gate. The traveller's journal on the approach also serves as an exact cave-door key.

Four independent favors give four distinct tokens: the frost thief's perfect snowflake for Sieck; Tookles' sunflower-petal pouch for Kithaya; Grielda's perfect dew drop for Kithapa; and the hollowed-out stump's perfect red leaf for Zialh. Each has its own delivery receipt and native experience reward. Narrated storms, daylight, spring ritual and decay are not extra checked milestones.

The red leaf lies at the top of the hollowed-out stump. Search for the secret, closed stump entrance and open it, or enter the dying stump from the clearing to reach the roots and climb. No personal harvest or leaf from another tree replaces the exact proof.

Offer one Spring, Autumn, Summer and Winter token together to the priestess in the dream tree for the fae key. Matching supplied tokens fit without your earlier personal favor receipts. Four copies of one season do not fit; receipts cannot restore spent tokens.

Search for the secret branches above the priestess, unlock the pickproof door with the fae key, and open the passage. The key has a declared break chance of one hundred percent, with actual destruction subject to accounting acceptance. From the ethereal branch, enter the shimmering portal to the Muse's court. Normal reciprocal unlocking/opening permits return, and the court has a down exit; reset/restart return episodes still need qualification.

Two instances of the imaginary friend follow the Spring and Summer children. Either accepts one obsidian rock for sunshine through the same outcome. Bitter sprites, an autumn satyr and autumn nymphs have declared rocks. The request narrates a skipping lesson without actually recording one.

Kyra accepts a lost-soul essence for decay. Eight initial satyr/sprite sources carry it; later same-named creatures do not all receive it. This is ordinary exact item proof, without a required player death or soul extraction. Sunshine and decay are potion rewards; drinking them is separate from delivery.

Bring twelve exact koi scales together to the fisherman for the necklace. Fifteen fish-and-scale declarations provide sufficient declared quantity across the brook; live supply is not guaranteed. He retires after acceptance. Currents and falling at the waterfall affect access; fishing text does not define an actual catch objective.

Larissa's description asks for the diamond-encrusted wand. It lies on the birch tree's thin ice floor in winter; that room and its upper canopy can cause falling. Return this exact wand to her for the diamond stud. Wandering encounter and first recovery need their own evidence.

The waterfall object responds to jump waterfall and leads to the still cave. Two secret, locked, pickable cave doors use the traveller's journal and the perfect dew drop as exact keys, despite locket-shaped prose clues. Door code accepts those objects without requiring key item type. Use the dew gate before offering that copy if desired; cave exploration is optional and does not block supplied seasonal tokens.

The ledge below the Pegasus cliff has an enter seasonal portal to the Wheel of Time, then the dream tree. World-file value four alone is not a secret exit: the loader masks door type and reset commands set secrecy. Passage, secret discovery, portal arrival and survival are guidance rather than journal credit.

Fiera's shop sells an ordinary apple. Sieck, Pegasus and Kyra have shared class-matched level/runestone guidance from their teacher flags, without local epic-teaching contracts. The Muse, poetic lore and Zialh's elk heart do not supply a reviewed finale. Some seasonal tokens and the diamond stud have pickup-trap metadata; intended trap values and safe retrieval need qualification, not extra achievements.

story_mappings.introduction: Explore the Caverns of the Worms and bring exact skins and hides to Wilms for equipment. His sixteen independent commissions are supporting crafting services. New discovery and progress require active, ready accounting.
orientation: Enter from the Underdark and follow the short duergar corridor to the old tool alcove. Wilms is the curer who offers equipment for worm skins and hides. ASK wilms about cure, hide or wormskin, then use the listed equipment topics to hear his recipes. Recognized dialogue reveals the contact; each keyword is not a separate achievement.

The burrows contain grey, glowing, brown, red and purple worms. Small worms supply strips, middle-sized worms supply pieces and large worms supply whole hides. These exact colors and sizes are different materials; a hide cannot stand in for several strips or pieces. Exploration has several overlapping routes rather than a required personal quest order.

Choose the equipment you want and gather its complete bundle loose in inventory. Repeated ingredients require separate items together. The shield needs five items, the armor needs three separate red strips and two hides, and the mask, cloak and gloves need matching pairs. The journal shows current quantities; spent, nested, held or worn materials are not ready now.

ASK describes a recipe but does not select an order. If several complete bundles share an offered material, Wilms accepts the first matching complete request. Extra materials can make a larger or different commission take precedence. Keep only the intended complete bundle available when practical, and inspect the received equipment. A journal card does not reserve materials or select the native hand-in.

Some materials serve several commissions. Grey strip and red hide can make a helmet or contribute to a backpack; glowing strip can make an ear clasp or combine with purple strip for a ring. The shield overlaps the boots ingredients. Choose how to spend your stock; receiving equipment is separate from having materials ready for another commission.

A small fixed pile of garbage conceals a blocked passage in the red burrows. PUSH the garbage to affect the south passage toward the purple worm route. A passage another player already opened is usable without your own earlier solve. The garbage stays fixed and is separate from Wilms's ingredient requests.

Bring light for the dark burrows and respect normal movement, combat and access rules. Wet descriptions do not by themselves require swimming or flight. The Underdark entrance is south from the entry cavern despite its old description; the deeper connector route is separate. An incoming veil can also arrive here, but using it is not a required step.

Exact supplied skins and hides fit without your own earlier kills, source recovery, tunnel visits, dialogue or control history. Accepting a commission records its independent service receipt; owning its reward alone does not prove acceptance. These services do not add quest achievements or dailies. Discovery remains a separate achievement, and new credit requires active, ready accounting.

story_mappings.introduction: Trace the five plaza-statue routes and exact Glory Badges to Lothrell’s memorial and lesser bloodsaber, then choose the caecilia upgrade, unicorn-horn key, minotaur letter and ooze branches or Willem’s named-skull reward. Access guidance and supplied shortcuts remain separate from accepted quest outcomes.
orientation: The ruined city has open approaches from the Surface grasslands and Turolopolis Zoo. Lothrell’s active source is outside the city in the Surface’s grassy fertile foothills; his historical Verspin account does not place him there today. Discovering or meeting him on the Surface does not discover the ruined city.

Lothrell wants one each of the brown, green, blue, red and black Glory Badges, together. Five copies of one colour and the white badge do not replace the five exact colours. The carriers are living trapped heroes; the accepted memorial alone does not record personal rescue.

RUB the plaza’s statues to enter the five mirrored rooms. Their five badge keys open separate hatches: red up, black south, blue north, green east and brown west. SEARCH for a secret local hatch, UNLOCK it with the matching badge, then OPEN and travel. ENTER each room’s portal for a return to the centre of the Plaza of Statues. Keep needed badges for travel before giving all five to Lothrell.

The lesser bloodsaber from Lothrell can be paired with the sewer caecilia’s exact hidden stinger for Kurtukr’s upgrade. A supplied lesser blade skips that earlier route; the five-badge receipt cannot replace a blade already spent or handed away. Kurtukr follows Sprecken through holding-room dispersal, so find the actual surviving recipient.

SEARCH the shop’s lower passage or the restaurant’s secret trapdoor, OPEN it and enter the sewer. Falls above the park, beneath the flophouse, by sewer debris and at the palace chandelier can interrupt intended movement. A handled portal command, a fall or a found passage is separate from accepted arrival and source recovery.

The minotaur’s timeworn letter serves the drow emissary. His blue-ooze request gives wrappings, then removes him and his remaining possessions; killing him for the letter also removes that current ooze recipient. Plan letter recovery or a supplied copy before choosing the ooze outcome. Only one of the blue-ooze placements carries the exact blue lump.

Corwyck’s exact unicorn horn earns an iron bunker key, while one palace sentinel carries the separate crimson palace key. The jailor’s key serves four pickable cell doors. These keys normally break after successful unlocks, so reset locks may need another copy. Unlock, open, recovery and the accepted offering are distinct actions.

Willem’s loaded named skull earns the slave’s coin reward. Ordinary carved parts do not replace the exact horn, stinger or skull. Current supplies and accepted offerings do not prove a personal source kill, first recovery, rescue, fountain cleansing or collapse of the palace’s spell field. Questions and book chapters guide you without an achievement for every keyword.

Exact supplied ingredients remain valid. Cap-one stock, recipient departure, rare dispersal and traps can limit a journey; daily metadata does not promise renewal. Every new discovery, encounter, journal, achievement and daily credit requires active, ready accounting; frozen reward recovery remains separate.

story_mappings.introduction: Explore an obsidian city, its market and temple, hidden tunnels, wizardry tower, harbor and royal keep. Eight independent accepted deliveries explain the courtship, relic, royal recipe and conspiracy routes. A custom moonstone story spans foreign sources and ship services, with no invented completion. Active, ready accounting is required; source, custom settlement, access and retiring-recipient qualification remain open.
orientation: Ordinary boundaries lead from the valley road to the city gates, from the harbor to the surface bay, and from the underground tunnels to the underworld river cavern. Administrative loading-room exits are separate; arrival prose does not establish a safe return journey.

The courtship material route is exact obsidian fragment → ornate silver dagger → sealed letter → two different blue items. Each accepted exchange is independent. Supplied matching materials fit without earlier receipts; ordinary shop daggers, potions or scrolls do not substitute.

The revenge/relic route is exact steel lockpicks → ancient fragile sword → magical dust and cloak. Dialogue calls lockpicks proof of death, but neither possession nor acceptance checks a personal kill. The romance and revenge routes are not mutually exclusive in the native contracts.

The royal recipe takes three items together: local dragon stomach, Ice Crag root vial and dusty ampoule. The foreign vial is produced by an onion delivery. Delivery gives an obsidian badge and retires the royal recipient; it does not certify an invasion or demonic neutralization.

A separate palace token delivery takes a Peacekeeper badge for two scrolls. The advisor recipe then takes magical formulas, a demon heart, magical dust and the sparkling blue token together. Royal and conspiracy receipts are independent; no poisoning, succession or campaign-wide branch state is recorded.

The two blue rewards differ: the sparkling item is a generic quest material with no potion spells, while the light-blue leather flask is a real potion. Native prose about permanent sight and a sleeping potion needs a builder decision; custody never proves those effects happened.

The market obsidian fragment has a one-copy, forty-chance source; sources and recipients may be missing in an episode. Three recipients retire after acceptance. Eight static daily candidates do not guarantee an available daily journey or unlimited repeated supply.

Temple silver-key custody, hidden basement and tunnel doors, royal obsidian-key doors, maze travel and harbor services are separate prerequisites. A carried or equipped key alone cannot prove successful unlock, passage or return. The underground dragon source can wander.

A custom artificer in the wizardry tower wants a finished moonstone. To assemble the heart, carry exactly two fragments and one core loose in your inventory and allow them time to combine. One fragment is seeded on a foreign automaton; another is placed on the water-plane princess or in the sea vault; the pirate ship treasure chest is the declared custom core source. The pirate ship is deliberately disabled with accounting active, so a fresh core cannot currently be recovered there.

The custom moonstone path offers a ring or ship crew as alternative uses of the same stone. The crew needs an owned ship, at least 3000 ship frags and 40000000 copper. Broken pieces provoke an attack. A separate foreign three-item commission also consumes a finished moonstone; earlier assembly history does not preserve the stone. Assembly, accepted payment, ring issuance and crew installation have no native journal binding; current materials do not award those outcomes.

Local lore, shop stock, teacher/tradeskill declarations, bank notices, crew hiring and rent remain separate from the eight deliveries. Conversations and reward choices with the artificer are explained here, but their completion is not yet recorded by the journal. Some mount-shop stock is missing and needs restoration.

Optional producer receipts describe a route, while current material checks describe present unequipped custody. Neither distinguishes personal first recovery from gifts, verifies a source kill or combines independent exchanges into a finished campaign.

story_mappings.introduction: Follow the apprentices’ notes, decode the rune doors and explore the Citadel’s guarded treasures. Two independent accepted deliveries record outcomes. The unfinished empty contract is excluded. New discovery and progress require active, ready accounting.
orientation: Arrive at the drawbridge from the shadowed forest. Examine the plaque beside the onyx door. SAY paradox unlocks the northern entrance; OPEN it afterward if closed. Speech ability and existing shared door state still matter. The inside return starts closed, without the outside lock.

The wandering apprentice asks for a bluish key and promises information. His accepted exchange pays 50 platinum and retires that particular giver; the reply admits he knows nothing. He has many starting placements and can wander. This is a delivery outcome, without a teleport or learning objective for you.

The grumbling apprentice in the arctic greenhouse wears a heavy coat. Its pockets contain the bluish key. The key fits the chest behind the washroom’s concealed western door on the apprentice floor. A supplied key fits too, and the chest is not pickproof. Opening it is separate from spending the key on the wandering apprentice’s reward.

The concealed-room chest contains the exact sheets of notes and a ruby ring. The notes discuss the runes and riddles. Keep the notes directly carried for the lost apprentice near the Master’s chambers. Loose custody can show current preparation; it does not prove who recovered them or how the chest was opened.

Ask the arctic apprentice about runes, decipher, doors, secret and riddles. Find Growler’s Book of Runes in the library and the Book of Riddles carried by the philosophy professor. LOOK page1, page2 and the other pages for clues. Hearing or reading a clue does not record a separate quest achievement.

The four runed store-room doors use spoken words: wind at the north-facing rune, dark at the east-facing rune, black at the other north-facing rune and time at the west-facing rune. SAY the word beside its door, then OPEN it if needed. The magic unlocks matching reciprocal doors too. An already-open path does not require your own password action.

Amberyl’s ghost and lyre occupy one guarded inner room. Her books describe the lyre’s price and her lingering sorrow. The amber key she carries fits the lyre’s locked display case and has a native chance of breaking on use. Taking the lyre does not record freeing the ghost or performing a song.

Twelve treasure vaults have twelve different keys carried by their elemental guardians. Their contents include four keys to further store rooms, a paper boat, phantom boots, diamond, flask, ring, earring, katana and mask. Preserve each exact key and destination; carrying one generic vault key does not open every vault.

The upper landing’s translation says to cry master, while the actual magical door currently responds to SAY shalafi. This mismatch needs a builder decision. The stone Guardian’s Key fits the Master’s study and sleeping-chamber doors; the Master’s paradox key leads onward, and the Portal Guardian’s golden key fits the nightstone vault.

The lost apprentice asks in dialogue for his notes and all twelve vault treasures. The implemented reward checks only the exact notes and gives a very small key; he remains afterward. The journal follows that accepted recipe. It does not require twelve extra items, claim that you rescued him or invent a completed glyph study.

The very small key fits the very small chest on the desk in the sleeping chambers. Its native break setting is 100 percent after successful unlocking; the chest is pickproof. Its two necklace children each have a 35 percent reset chance, and its rune wand has a 100 percent chance, subject to caps and reset conditions. A key receipt does not guarantee chest contents or a personal opening.

The final vault’s beholder carries ordinary equipment, a Citadel memory and a separately guarded epic stone. The large church door in its stock is equipment with a RUB glass effect when worn, rather than a travel portal. Teachers, combat, books, spell effects and epic rewards have their own rules; they are separate from the two delivery outcomes.

The trailing empty request has an item-zero goal, no response and no reward. It is excluded from achievement and daily credit pending builder review. Native definitions and any historical evidence remain intact. Both usable deliveries are potential dailies only when their actual giver and legitimate current proof stock are available; no reset or new progress is promised without active, ready accounting.

story_mappings.introduction: Discover the Caverns of Armageddon, meet the Hunters and follow fifteen independent bounties, the prisoner’s two companies, Blicatch’s four creature parts and the Dragon Queen’s two-amulet upgrade. Source clues explain actual locks, containers, secret routes and foreign follow-ups; accepted named exchanges remain separate from the wider campaign.
orientation: Active, ready accounting is required for discovery, visible NPC encounters, journals and new achievement/daily credit. First discovery is its own achievement. Reading hints and current material checks award no credit.

The forest connects to the Jade Empire surface. Xavier’s forest portal reaches the Myrabolus observatory backroom; its destination still has a sealed door. The native west forest boundary is not reciprocal with the inbound surface edge, so a return route must be qualified separately.

The mercenary camp’s fifteen bounties are independent. Ask each actual recipient orc or orcs for lore; keyword questions do not themselves record achievements. Most recipients are fixed, but Clond and Redana can move. Roland has a valid bounty recipe but no active declared reset placement in the scanned world; resolve his availability before assigning the Maximas bounty as a daily. Starting-room clues are not evidence of a current actor.

The ordinary shaft entrance requires the steel key carried by its elite orc. Graiven’s closed blood basin contains the chipped rock key for the locked east steps beyond Veannan. The guard captain has the stone key for the general cavern’s locked east entrance. These keys have zero normal-unlock break chance; current possession is optional route guidance, not proof of opening or arrival.

Proofs are loaded NPC inventory objects, not automatically severed heads or generated death callbacks. Scralack’s head comes from the Jade Empire’s strike-force general. Exact loose-carried kinds are required; equipped, held, nested or merely similar proof does not satisfy the native offering search. Supplied proof is accepted without a personal kill or original-source history.

Open the wounded Myrabolan soldier, dying Soldier of Fortune or dying Wild Card container as appropriate to recover two different company-tag kinds. These are object containers, not wounded NPC healing or escort missions. The prisoner exchange has no native disappearance command even though its prose describes leaving.

Blicatch’s secret stone entrance leads into a chamber whose northern return is blocked; continue south into the ogre station for the ordinary route. Archangel wings have a one-charge GET/PUT sleep trap; an attempted pickup can trigger sleep without recovering the wings. A wyvern wing is not a substitute.

The archangel, behemoth, beholder and Krazzi’s following fire elemental supply Blicatch’s four different parts. His accepted reward gives both amulets and retires him. Reset mode one permits native repeatable classification but does not prove a currently admitted NPC or replacement materials.

The Dragon Queen combines one kilospanatis amulet and one hazy blue amulet into the cosmos amulet. Her native acceptance does not require your Blicatch history. Alexis in Myrabolus can supply the hazy blue amulet for a treasure chest. Earlier receipts do not recreate consumed amulets.

Argophel’s lair is below the secret grate at the golem intersection. Maximas is below the secret waterfall passage. The general’s rift uses ENTER and reaches the downward spiral; no ordinary reverse portal is declared there. Defeating Endosa is lore and a bounty source, not an enforced receipt prerequisite for entering.

Maverick and Abbadon share the throne room. The secret rescue ladder goes up to the Sunweaver; the reverse descent into the throne room is blocked. From the airship’s other ladder descend to the forest, with no ordinary ascent back. These static routes do not certify rescuing actors or winning a campaign.

Abbadon’s cosmos key opens both the secret temple vault wall and the locked, pickproof statue in Ajax’s part of the forest. Its normal-unlock break chance is one hundred percent. One successful use can consume a key, so do not assume the same physical key opens both locks; renewed or shared supply requires qualification. The Soulsword is in the vault; the ring of abnormal power is in the statue. Neither is a local accepted quest terminal.

The Sunweaver has four treasure-chest object placements in two rooms, subject to their shared cap. They are quest objects, not openable containers. Myrabolus recipients Rico, Random, Decker and Alexis accept chests for separate rewards. The lost monkey atop the redwood goes to Myrabolus’s monkey hunter; Abbadon’s heart goes to the Sky City of Ultarium’s dwarven trapper. Foreign receipts remain credited to their real zones.

Imported epic rune and memory objects in the general’s rift chamber use their existing systems. The magical fountain in the throne room uses a rotating spell pool on DRINK; it is not an escape portal or accepted quest. Existing settlement and effects need committed outcome integration, not another payout or invented keyword credit.

All eighteen native exchanges remain separate named outcomes. All retain native daily shape, including Blicatch under reset mode one. Actual difficulty, source-generation admission, current stock, secret access, traps, group eligibility and renewal still need qualification before daily assignment. Active accounting refuses legacy item resets without admitted generation.

The sources contain broader claims about exorcising Maverick, immortal Hunters, army defeat, delayed rescue and using the Soulsword against gods. No local assigned procedure or shipped trigger establishes those campaign transitions. Record these as future builder-selected objectives, with committed events and clear scope, before claiming a completed campaign.

contacts.description: At the reception library of Bone Fort Inn. Ask about hi, books, guests and boots. He needs all four different books together; the bookrack is not their source.
contacts.name: a hunched man

contacts.description: In the village blacksmith’s hut, east of the village path. Ask about hi, scales or dragon. His red-scales AND 500-platinum order is currently unavailable with active accounting.
contacts.name: a barbarian blacksmith

contacts.description: May emerge from a branching loading route into the ice forest. Ask about hi, boots or boot, malinar and sword. Her boots and head exchanges are independent; she leaves after the head exchange.
contacts.name: Eleadora, guardian of the ice forest

contacts.description: In the fisherman’s home behind the locked western flap near the starving barbarian. Ask hi. A fishbone key from feeding the barbarian opens the flap and breaks on ordinary successful unlocking. Exact supplied materials do not require an earlier feeding receipt.
contacts.name: a barbarian shaman

contacts.description: At the bend beside the locked western flap to the shaman’s home. Ask hi, hello or hey. Needs a clam AND pike AND lobster together; gives the fishbone key.
contacts.name: a starving barbarian

contacts.description: Two strange-looking guests begin in inn bedrooms. Only the one in the far western bedroom starts carrying the hidden dark green book.
contacts.name: a strange guest

contacts.description: Two shady travellers begin in inn bedrooms. Only the one with the working mirror starts carrying the hidden dark magenta book. PUSH that mirror opens the blocked northern passage.
contacts.name: a shady traveller

contacts.description: Two human travellers begin in inn bedrooms. Only the one in the western bedroom nearest the stairs starts carrying the old book.
contacts.name: a human traveller

contacts.description: At the inn entrance, starts carrying the hidden dark black book. Other travellers and duplicate guests do not substitute for this fourth kind.
contacts.name: a dark traveller

contacts.description: May reach the fire-beaten cave below the inn through its loading route. Starts carrying hidden red dragon scales. Scales recovery, personal victory and paid armor preparation are different facts.
contacts.name: a thundering red dragon

contacts.description: May emerge into the icy tundra from branching loading rooms. Starts with his own exact bloody head already carried. His rare grey giant boots do not satisfy Eleadora’s snowy adventurer boots request.
contacts.name: Malinar, blood enemy of Eleadora

contacts.description: At the end of the village path beside the locked northern flap to the fishmonger’s hut. Carries the hidden small wooden key. Her qc_action80 complaint is ambient dialogue, not an asked keyword or separate quest.
contacts.name: an angry barbarian wife

contacts.description: In the fisherman’s hut behind the locked northern flap. The wife’s wooden key fits that flap and breaks on ordinary successful unlocking. His selling prose has no configured shop binding or accepted exchange.
contacts.name: a barbarian fishmonger

contacts.description: At the small general store reached from the snowy crossing or the Surface highway. Sells rations, water, a backpack, potions and bandages. Rations do not replace the three required seafood kinds.
contacts.name: a barbarian-human halfbreed

contacts.description: May reach the ancient workshop behind the Ice Lounge’s visible closed southern door through a loading route. His invasion plans and laboratory are context; no local accepted invasion or research quest is bound.
contacts.name: Ixarvonl, the great illithid alchemist

contacts.description: At the Ice Lounge below the Onyx Stairs. Open the visible closed southern door to the ancient workshop. The bartender has no configured shop or accepted exchange.

story_mappings.introduction: Recover Bone Fort Inn’s four stolen books, follow the snowy boots to Eleadora, help the hungry village and deliver foreign materials to its shaman. Keep exact item kinds, optional supply routes, two different keys and Eleadora’s departure visible while exploring the tundra.
orientation: Bone Fort Inn’s hunched man accepts four different books together for snowy adventurer boots. Eleadora accepts those exact boots for glowing ice leggings and independently accepts Malinar’s bloody head for the tundra sword. The shaman’s fire gland and shell requests are two independent outcomes; feeding the barbarian needs three different seafood kinds together.

Follow the Surface highway entrance into Bone Fort Inn, open the northern bone door and go west into reception. The stairs north of the lobby go down to the Onyx Stairs. Western bedrooms hold the old, magenta and green books on different travellers; the dark traveller near the entrance holds the black book. Other copies of those guests begin without books.

The northern door at the Onyx Stairs is visible and closed despite the secret-passage description. Open it to reach the passages behind the rooms. Bedroom back doors are generally secret through their resets. In the shady traveller’s bedroom, PUSH the working mirror to open the blocked north passage; the mirrors described in other bedrooms are scenery.

Below the passage’s grate is the underground river, with sharks and an actual water sector. The dragon may emerge into the fire-beaten cave after its loading branch; it is not guaranteed to appear. Red scales support the blacksmith’s paid service. Open the Ice Lounge’s visible closed southern door to Ixarvonl’s workshop; SEARCH is not required and no research or invasion outcome is bound.

Eleadora and Malinar may emerge into the forest or tundra, or become inaccessible in loading branches. Find the actual actor when present. Return the snowy adventurer boots before giving Eleadora the head if you want both rewards in the same encounter: she leaves after the head exchange. These are independent receipts, without a forced boots-before-head requirement.

Feed the starving barbarian a small clam, a large pike and an impressive lobster together. His fishbone key unlocks the western flap to the shaman’s home and breaks on ordinary successful unlocking. That reward and the shaman’s later fire gland or shell receipts remain separate; public access or supplied items do not require personal feeding history.

FISH requires fishing skill, a recognised pole and a usable water room. The village’s Fishing Docks are coded as land; the name alone does not make FISH work there. The inn’s underground river is water but hazardous. Bom Fitherwood in Harrow trades a painting for a pike, lobster and hairy crab: you still need a clam. Foreign paid fish purchases remain unavailable while accounting is active.

The snapjaw turtle shell and fire gland come from foreign loaded creatures. Ship-yard dispersal sources and the Crimson Fulgur provide both kinds; Alatorin bladeback pyrolisks provide fire glands. Remove a worn shell or gland before offering it. Supplying either exact item is valid without your own kill, source journey or earlier feeding receipt.

The wife’s small wooden key fits the separate locked northern flap to the fishmonger’s hut and breaks on ordinary successful unlocking. It does not replace the fishbone key. The wife’s complaint is ambient; the fishmonger has no configured shop, so do not rely on him to supply the seafood.

The general store sells rations, water, a backpack, potions and bandages. Iron rations support a different foreign Cairme exchange and do not satisfy the starving barbarian. The blacksmith’s scales AND 500-platinum service remains unavailable with active accounting and earns no zone achievement or daily credit.

Some crossing signs describe routes absent from the loaded exits. The southern mountain pass has no usable southern destination, and an eastern forest exit points to an inactive legacy map room. Use verified Surface entrances; the journal does not promise those unresolved routes or send you into loading rooms.

Carry exact materials loose. Worn, nested, spent or handed-away copies remain missing; earlier receipts never replace them. Questions and source recovery explain progress without granting every keyword an achievement. Only accepted exact exchanges record outcomes. All new discovery, encounter, journal, achievement and daily credit requires active, ready accounting; frozen reward recovery remains separate.

story_mappings.introduction: Follow the Way of the Faerie to Finn and Anna's cottage, then connect the living tree's heart to the ruined elven temple. Finn's signet and key and Celriya's family blade have distinct accepted outcomes. The glowing-ring and five-plane forge trades are supporting services. Active, ready accounting is required.
orientation: The side path from the mainland forest enters a looping enclosure. Find the southern hidden path from the large clearing, then follow it east through the foliage to the Way. The ordinary mainland return is west from that side path.

Meet Finn at the choice of directions below the hill. His native anna, ring/home and key/castle topics connect local routes without learned-keyword achievements. The dwarf and mischievous forest inhabitants are separate encounters.

Travel up and over the hill, then through the highland forest path to Anna's living oak cottage. Read the upstairs library entries for the lost city, Celriya and Finn. Anna has no addressed quest topics; her description points to this library.

The library advertises an orb return. Touch the actual orb to reach the realm's side path; travel west from there to the mainland forest. Orbs are also declared in the cottage heart. Touching is a travel action, not Finn's departure or an automatic quest milestone.

For a personal cottage route, Anna holds the white-metal key fitting the cellar trapdoor. The dangerous tunnels contain roots, no-magic sections and a floorless shaft. The tree spirit starts in an equipment load room and can wander into its chamber, where it blocks down while present.

Recover the tree spirit's worn signet for Finn. The accepted return gives a map and glowing ring. This preserves Finn's existing delivery and does not magically send him home. The spirit's amulet is a key for the temple tomb, not proof you killed it yourself.

The old southern roadway reaches the ruined city and temple garden. Say peace at its magical gate to unlock it, then open it. The two reflecting pools describe Oberon's final battle and Celriya's loss through static room text; they do not transport you into the past.

The ancient sword in the cottage heart is Tvelor's family artifact. A tablet in the goblin's junk heap explains the connection. Bring the sword to Celriya for faerie-sight goggles and her restoration wand; she retires after acceptance. The goggles are a reward, without a reviewed mandatory quest gate.

Carry or hold the tree spirit amulet to unlock the temple tomb slab. Oberon carries Finn's mammoth castle key. Returning that key gives Finn's sword and 500,000 copper and retires his current appearance; no earlier ring exchange is required.

Finn calls his other input a teleport scroll, but his binding actually consumes the glowing ring for a map and 500 copper. Fulbar's shop wall also describes a bulky travel scroll, while the actual stocked scroll identifies items. These content discrepancies await deliberate builder correction.

Two forge makers accept all five distinct planar parts and 5,000,000 copper for the same Fix scroll. They start in a dispersal network and can wander into distant areas. Item checks explain supplies; active accounting currently refuses the paid recipe until supported settlement.

Fix repairs the condition of one selected carried or equipped item in a separate scroll action. A maker receipt, a Moradin gift, an epic-store purchase or a supplied scroll does not prove you repaired something or recovered the five parts personally.

The library's golden-gate riddle is still an undetermined placeholder, and the gate has no destination. The lost Song, Mab's earlier restoration and waiting for Oberon to return also have no accepted local ending. Keep these as lore until builders choose implemented outcomes.

Current supplies remain optional preparation. Gifts are valid native inputs; previous receipts explain history without replacing spent materials. Only accepted native exchanges complete these named deliveries, and active sources, travel and recipient availability still need qualification.

story_mappings.introduction: Help the hermit, follow the tomb and word-puzzle clues, collect Surok’s five distinct adamantite chunks, and choose the jade statue’s trophy, token and collar exchanges. Keep personal investigation, current proof and recorded outcomes distinct.
orientation: The northern passage of the Undead Outpost leads EAST onto the Crypt’s forest trail. WEST from the trail returns there. Follow the trail around the graveyard to the hermit’s cabin. Burned bridge, river, lake, underwater passage and waterfall are real terrain; source metadata is not a promise of safe access.

Ask the hermit hello, hi, howdy or name for his request, hunting or hunt about game, and graveyard, strange, scared or tomb about the danger. Ask Surok hello, hi or name, or crypt, dungeon, catacomb or catacombs. The jade statue answers hello, hi, howdy or name without explaining its recipes. These six response families have twenty-one aliases; keywords are not individual achievements.

The hermit needs exactly four kindling sticks and two branches, all loose together. The many trail floor sources are different from the log, charred timber and other wood. He reveals a key-location clue and departs. The rusted tomb key already starts hidden on the eastern trail; no item reward, campfire action or personal hermit receipt is required to recover it.

The rusted key unlocks the northern tomb door. Inspect and PUSH the fixed gargoyle head to open the blocked downward slab. A loose-stone switch at the staircase opens the upward slab. These are actual shared controls, but the journal does not yet record personal operation or passage clearance.

The banquet-hall torch is a fixed PULL switch for the east wall into the scat pit. Nakral’s fixed bone throne is a PUSH switch opening the north passage into the earthen tunnel. The controls open their declared blocked exits; looking at a torch or throne, another player’s operation or an already-open passage is not your recorded action.

Three note fragments contain parts of the word puzzle: the mostly burnt note in charred embers, the scrap carried by the orc shaman, and the scrap carried by the tall dark creature. Read their descriptions and combine the fragments. SAY the combined word near the special iron door; the real magic-door handler unlocks it. Reading and successful unlocking currently have no personal durable journal milestone.

Surok in the morgue needs all five distinct adamantite chunks, one from each of the mapped sites. They look identical. Four are floor sources; the fifth is inside a locked wooden chest in a secret ironwood alcove. Same-name duplicates from another site cannot replace a missing kind. His four-or-five dialogue is only a clue; the accepted recipe is exactly five.

The jade statue’s first exchange uses iron butterfly wings, a black imp tail, a magma horn and a white wolf ear together for a stone token. The token can then be exchanged for a moss-covered bracelet. A supplied token fits without personal earlier trophy history; the earlier receipt never replaces the current token.

The imprisoned hell hound’s original mithril collar is a separate statue input for an enhanced collar. Input and reward have identical names but different identities. Token-to-bracelet and collar enhancement each make the statue depart. They are distinct outcomes that need a fresh recipient episode if you want both; the four-trophy exchange alone keeps it present.

Nakral’s journal has separate page17 and page24 descriptions explaining his research and moral decline. Other papers, formulae, corpses, scratchings, the imported father-spirit object and ordinary combat provide context. Reading, rescuing a prisoner, defeating a mutant or ending all experiments is not an invented accepted quest endpoint. The magical fountain has an existing shared drinking effect, separate from story credit.

The cavern’s authored UP exit points to an old surface room absent from the active world; the loader removes unresolved exits. Do not rely on that surface route. The fixed glowing orb near the old skeleton is an existing TOUCH return to the graveyard trail, subject to the shared travel rules. It remains non-takeable; no portable escape capability is added.

Current loose materials, earlier accepted receipts, original source, gifts, learned words, keys, switches, movement, combat, epic claims and final rewards are distinct facts. Five static daily candidates depend on real material and recipient renewal under native mode1; reset declarations do not prove availability. All new discovery, encounter, journal, achievement and daily credit requires active, ready accounting; frozen recovery is separate. No native zone repair or mobility change ships.

story_mappings.introduction: Explore the Transparent Tower, recover the scepter and follow three independent companion requests to the librarian's mist key. Four exchanges, fourteen contacts and eleven optional checks explain current native acceptance. Active, ready accounting is required. Supplied proofs fit; puzzle, source, defeat, epic-touch and escape objectives need separate accepted evidence.
orientation: Meet the actual recipients before using addressed ASK topics. Twenty-six dialogue families explain the tower, companions, books and escape. Words do not independently award quest credit or prove learning.

The ordinary scepter route uses the illithid's warped key, the white mist's swirl key, then Aceralde's marble key for the sitting-room desk. All four progression keys, including the later mist reward, have a hundred-percent normal-unlock break chance. Current carried keys are optional snapshots, not durable access history.

The scepter is placed inside a locked, pickproof white marble desk. Opening it triggers a three-charge room-wide acid trap. Take the exact scepter out into loose carried inventory before offering it. A supplied scepter bypasses this personal recovery route.

Gullivier, Devilish and Lisa independently accept the scepter kind, return that kind and give one identical pale purple token before departing. The returned scepter does not guarantee the same UID. Each request records only its own recipient outcome.

The librarian wants three tokens of that common kind plus the scepter together. Three unique sources, all three earlier personal receipts, a particular order, allegiance and defeating Aceralde are not native requirements. Supplied proofs remain valid.

Gullivier's green-door portal uses SOUTH into the field. Find the hidden downward grass route and eastern wall past the blue mist dragon. His return-tree portal uses SOUTH; eastward reward prose needs builder review.

Devilish's red-door portal uses SOUTH into Avernus. Beneath its tree is his chamber. SAY illusion at the iron door to unlock and reveal it, then OPEN it. The portal beyond returns on EAST; the purple obelisk instead returns on SCREAM.
Lisa's lower-stair open-book portal uses SOUTH into the shadow dragon cave. Open the hidden eastern door to her chamber. Her return-tree portal uses SOUTH.

The fountain's hidden west route leads to the descending slide and mist-covered library approach. A stair portal also sends WEST into the slide. READ the library room's book portal to reach the lower stair. Ordinary room exits alone do not describe every valid route.

After the librarian exchange, use the mist key at the green mist door from the lower stair. SAY reality at the secret wall, then OPEN it; the accepted word unlocks and reveals the reciprocal directions but leaves them closed. The closet portal uses SOUTH to the drawbridge.

The first door portal uses STARE, not LOOK; the field return uses CRY; book controls use their specified commands. Named controls must select the actual object. A successful command, travel arrival or return needs its own accepted event before becoming a story objective.

The closet's rune of blue power uses the shared durable epic-touch transaction. Its reward and group participation are separate from the token exchange and from actual escape. Story integration should consume its committed result, not a typed TOUCH or descriptive glow.

The globe of shadows and shadowcraft mace belong to tower prototypes but their active declared sources are foreign: the Chronomancer and Chernovog. Their actual artifact effects and the globe's pet benefit are separate from local quest rewards. Two trash prototypes carry a stone-effect binding without an active local source; builder intent remains pending.

One ordinary southern exit from the western stair reaches the drawbridge. This source route does not enforce the narrative's closet-only escape claim. Illusion-themed direction mismatches and escape policy need builder confirmation before native repairs.

All four exchanges remain separate story outcomes; only the librarian recipe has native daily shape. Retiring companions, reset mode one, shared supply, current access, actual encounters and active, ready accounting govern repeats. No full-tower rescue, epic-touch or escape achievement is invented.

story_mappings.introduction: Help Woodseer's musicians, makers, mages and cooks with seven independent item returns. Explore the park, hive and rivers for supplies, or bring a matching item supplied by another player. Discovery is separate. New progress requires active, ready accounting.
orientation: Woodseer has a walled halfling town, park and pond, shops and mage homes, a bee nest, river and farms, mine, mountain trails and outer jungle. Discovery starts your journal; safe access, available supplies and a present giver still matter.

ASK the wandering bard about instrument, play, park or mandolin. Look for his broken mandolin in the badger burrow below the park. Search for and open the boulder passage. Return the broken mandolin for 1,000 copper; Lomar's playable shop mandolin is a different item. The bard plans to repair it after the return.

ASK the woman in the farmer's cottage about searching, cupboard, recipe or honey. Look for honey on warrior bees in the hive, then return it for 500 copper. She suggests taking beeswax to a woodworker. You can complete either return first.

ASK the woodworker about beeswax, wax or polish. Look for wax on the queen bee. Return it for a wooden ring. You can bring matching wax supplied by another player; completing the honey return first is optional.

ASK the teaching mage about potion or potions. Look for a loose bee egg in the egg room above the queen's chamber, then return it for a potion. A matching supplied egg also fits. Using the potion is a separate action.

ASK the wizard about search, searching, components or feather. Look for the exact hummingbird feather on tiny hummingbirds around the park and town. The outer jungle's glowing feather is different. Return the correct feather for 500 copper, or bring a matching feather supplied by another player.

ASK the artist about pigment, pigments or green. Look for green pigment on giant dragonflies along the river. Bring the correct pigment for 500 copper. You can use matching supplied pigment without personally hunting a dragonfly.

ASK the maitre d' at The Quivering Leaf Restaurant about turtle or soup. Search snapping turtles in the large park and beneath the waterfall for raw turtle meat; other turtles may have none. Return the raw meat for turtle soup and 500 copper. The waiter's soup is a different item from the required meat.

Keep honey and raw meat uneaten, and keep each required item loose in your inventory. Worn, held, nested, consumed or handed-away items are unavailable for the return. Carrying the item prepares a request. Your journal records completion when the giver accepts it; owning a reward or learning a clue does not complete the request.

The bartender in Mathorn's bar also offers world-quest assignments. Those assignments are separate from these seven item returns. The pet shop and inn are optional services. Pet buying and rental are currently unavailable while active accounting is enabled.

Woodseer's fish merchant sells a salmon steak sought by a hermit in the Surface minizones. The hermit asks for both the steak and a firebreather. That return belongs to the hermit's zone; buying or carrying a steak alone does not complete it.

All seven returns can contribute achievements and potential dailies. The bard and woodworker leave after acceptance, so another visit needs a present giver and fresh supplies. River currents, falls, guards and shared doors still affect access. A new daily does not guarantee stocked supplies.
